title.narrative: Emergency agriculture and nutrition response to support the most vulnerable population in Al Mukha and Misrakh districts of Taiz Governorate

description.narrative: Out of the 16 governorates recording returnees and vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs), FAO will utilize this Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) allocation for under-funded emergencies in Yemen to support vulnerable smallholder farming households in Al Makha and Al Misrakh Districts in Taiz Governorate. Th In Al Makha district, the Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate stands at 30.8%, while in Al Misrakh it is 13%. According to WHO thresholds, these rates are classified as extremely critical" and "serious," respectively. According to FAO’s September 2024 high frequency monitoring, 60% of the population in Taiz Governorate are experiencing poor food consumption gaps. Food insecurity is a major driver of malnutrition in Yemen. Malnutrition among children and women is a serious public health problem among children, pregnant and lactating women in the targeted locations. Malnourished children, particularly those with severe acute malnutrition, have a higher risk of death from common childhood illness, such as diarrhea and pneumonia. Nutrition-related factors contribute to about 45% of deaths among children under 5 years of age. In Yemen, sub-optimal access to quality diets, as well as the lack of knowledge to prepare and consume dietary diversified meals, are major drivers of malnutrition. The overall objective of this proposal is to improve the food security and nutritional well-being of the most vulnerable farming households by providing emergency agricultural assistance and fostering better nutrition awareness. The expected outcome of the proposed intervention is to reduce the impact of food insecurity and malnutrition among the most vulnerable households whilst progressively transitioning to more resilient and sustainable livelihoods. FAO’s support will be channeled through a cash plus approach, which includes the provision of in-kind crop and livestock inputs together with season-specific cash assistance. Time-sensitive emergency livelihood interventions, especially when combined with cash assistance, have demonstrated a significant positive impact on health and nutrition outcomes.The project will support 2,700 vulnerable smallholder farming households (18,900 individuals) from the host communities, IDPs and returnees. The project will target 1,000 households (7,000 individuals) in the district of Al Makha and 1,700 (11,900 individuals) in Al Misrakh. 1,500 households (500 in Al Makha and 1000 in Al Misrakh) will receive cash + vegetable seeds (tomatoes, onions, okra, mallow and hot pepper seeds) and agriculture tools and 1,200 households will receive livestock packages composed of live animals, animal feed and mineral blocks. The Cash+ approach will support beneficiaries receiving crop inputs by improving their food access until the vegetable harvest season. All project beneficiaries will receive training on best practices for crop and livestock production, along with awareness sessions on nutrition to optimize the management of project inputs and improve beneficiaries’ nutrition’ nutrition knowledge.
